Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I'll reason as this farmer, then give you the structured plan.

---

**My thinking this season**

I got 8 mu, that's all. With 7 mouths at home and only some of us working outside, I can't afford a bad year. My oldest boy sends money from the city sometimes, but I don't count on it. I do wheat then maize same as always, same as everyone on our side of the village. My father did it, I do it.

For wheat — I'll plant in early October when the soil moisture is right, same as every year. I save some seed from last harvest but I also buy a bit of new seed from the agro shop, the clerk said it's good for our area. Before plowing I put down compound fertilizer, about 2 bags for the whole 8 mu — that's the 15-15-15 kind, maybe 40 kg per mu. Then at jointing when the wheat is coming up green in spring, I topdress urea, about half a bag per mu. My neighbor Old Wang uses more but he has a better well. I water three times usually — once before winter so the roots settle, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. If spring rain comes I skip one, saves on the electric bill for the pump. Last year I got maybe 420 kg per mu, year before was 450, I hope for 420 again.

For maize — soon as wheat is off in June, I got no time. I hire the neighbor with the no-till planter, he charges 25 yuan per mu and drops the seed right into the wheat stubble. Same day or next day. I use a hybrid seed, everyone does now, the old varieties don't yield. Base fertilizer goes down with the seed, then I topdress urea when it's knee-high. Maize needs less water than wheat usually, the summer rain helps. Maybe one or two waterings if July is dry. Last year I got around 450 kg per mu.

Pesticide — I spray herbicide after planting both crops, otherwise weeds take over. For bugs I only spray if I see them. Can't afford to spray for nothing.

Money-wise, I figure I'll spend about 4,500-5,000 yuan total on both crops for the whole 8 mu. That's tight but it's what I have. If wheat prices are good at harvest I might buy a bit more topdress for maize, otherwise I stretch.
